QUESTION:
What are the most common adverse reactions to Prednisone?

RESPONSE:
The label excerpt you provided does not include a dedicated “Adverse Reactions” section. However, the Dosage & Administration text discusses the common undesirable effects of systemic corticosteroid (prednisone) therapy. These include: pituitary‑adrenal (HPA) suppression; Cushingoid features (eg, central/centripetal obesity, thinning of the skin, easy bruisability); muscle wasting and weakness; hypertension; latent diabetes/hyperglycemia; osteoporosis; electrolyte imbalances; growth suppression in children; and corticoid withdrawal symptoms. The label also notes that long‑term pharmacologic dosing can produce the clinical findings of hyperadrenocorticism. For a complete list of adverse reactions and their frequencies, consult the full prescribing information or the product’s “Adverse Reactions” section.
